threat.doubling_time_notes: Early Wuhan case doubling time 7.4 days (95% CI 4.2-14) up to Jan 4 2020. Use with L.logistic only for case growth inside one city; the points below are the better on-screen curve.
threat.notes: extent = share of the 234 non-aggregate countries/territories in the OWID/WHO file with at least one confirmed case (a proxy for geographic spread; reporting dates lag real introductions). Aggregates (World, continents, income groups, EU) excluded. The 2 'countries' at Jan 5 are as the WHO-derived file reports them.

aggregation.notes: Days from t0 until the assembled solution (a vaccine dose) first reached each country: computed from OWID vaccinations.csv as the first date with total_vaccinations > 0, across 217 countries/territories (OWID aggregates excluded). p10 = Dec 28 2020, median = Feb 24 2021, p90 = May 4 2021; earliest Dec 4 2020 (Latvia, likely a trial/reporting artifact), latest day 658 (Oct 2021).

deploy.notes: Days from a country's first dose to 10% of its population having at least one dose (people_vaccinated_per_hundred >= 10), median across 212 countries; 5 countries with first doses never reached 10% in the data.

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. Design was already fast: RATES.md 'Science example' shows the vaccine sequence finalized 2 days after the genome was shared, so AI cannot claim much there, and clinical trials and manufacturing are bounded by biology and factories, not routing. The large spread is in distribution: RATES.md 'Vaccine distribution inequity' (0.2% of doses to low-income countries by May 2021, advocacy analysis). The counterfactual assumes only that better coordination lets the median country get first doses as early as the fastest 10% actually did (p10 = day 363), i.e. ~58 days sooner for the median country. It does not assume more vaccine was made.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: The threat reached 64% of countries by day 75 and ~88% by day 96; the assembled answer reached the median country on day 421, about 4.4x slower, with an 18-week spread between the fastest and slowest tenth.
